messages:
maria: Heads up — I just noticed several prod snapshot uploads that have no SSE/CMEK metadata in the object headers. Found from the audit query for uploads this morning.

backup-bot: detected PUT s3://snapshots/prod/2025-06-01/abc123 size=1.2GB headers={} user=svc-backup-uploader
backup-bot: detected PUT s3://snapshots/prod/2025-06-01/def456 size=900MB headers={} user=svc-backup-uploader

maria: No x-amz-server-side-encryption / x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id for those. That's a problem for compliance.

dan: @kevin did anything land on the uploader role today? :rotating_light:

kevin: I trimmed some permissions from svc-backup-uploader to reduce blast radius. I removed a broad kms:* allow and scoped it. I thought uploads used SSE-S3 though. Did we flip to CMEK?

sasha: We moved to CMEK for snapshot buckets 3 weeks ago (vault CMK arn:aws:kms:...) — the uploader must be explicitly allowed kms:Encrypt on that CMK, otherwise S3 will accept the object but metadata isn't set correctly by our agent.

maria: Audit timeline: 11:34–11:42 UTC, 4 PUTs. All from backup-uploader. Looks like the RBAC change happened at 11:30 (PR 5421).

kevin: Ok — my bad. I misread the overlay. I can push a narrow grant back for kms:Encrypt on that CMK for svc-backup-uploader. Will do a rollback ACL in 10m and post the IAM diff.

aaron: Meanwhile we should prevent restores from these objects until we verify. Patch to snapshot-restore service to reject objects missing SSE metadata? Quick guard.

maria: Strong agree. Aaron — can you add a preflight check in restore path to fail if head-object shows no ServerSideEncryption field? Quick snippet:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket snapshots --key prod/2025-06-01/abc123 --query 'ServerSideEncryption'
# returns null for affected objects
```

dan: Also add an alert rule on our audit logs: any s3 PUT to snapshots bucket with missing encryption header -> Pager. We missed that signal.

backup-bot: scan run queued by maria: ./scripts/scan_unencrypted_snapshots.sh --since 2025-06-01T00:00Z
backup-bot: sample output:
prod/2025-06-01/abc123 , 2025-06-01T11:34:22Z , svc-backup-uploader
prod/2025-06-01/def456 , 2025-06-01T11:36:07Z , svc-backup-uploader

sasha: If we re-grant kms:Encrypt, future uploads will be fine but existing objects are not transparently re-encrypted. We have two options: 1) re-upload the snapshot (if uploader retained local copy / pipeline), or 2) copy the object server-side with proper SSE-KMS header to create a new encrypted copy. Both require access to the plaintext or to re-copy via S3 control-plane with the CMK.

kevin: I'll open an emergency PR to add kms:Encrypt for svc-backup-uploader with a condition limiting it to snapshots bucket and the CMK ARN. Will tag for fast review.

maria: Action items:
- kevin: submit IAM patch + rollback log (ETA 15m)
- dan: add Datadog/Splunk alert for missing SSE metadata on PUTs (ETA 30m)
- aaron: add restore preflight guard (ETA 1h)
- sasha: enumerate affected snapshots & advise on practical re-encrypt/re-upload path, plus customer-impact check (ETA 2h)
- maria: update encryptops playbook + postmortem template (ETA EOD)

dan: Also recommend we add an automated CI gate for permission changes that touch uploader roles when CMEK is enabled — flag CMK usage and require security ack.

kevin: Agreed. Sorry team, I over-optimized. Will coordinate with you all. :bow:

sasha: Also add an audit rule for KMS policy changes that remove Encrypt/Decrypt on keys with tags "managed:snapshots" — that would've flagged the PR.

maria: I'll escalate to incidents channel if we detect customer-visible restores failing. For now, we're triaging internally.

backup-bot: scan complete — 4 objects unencrypted, all within the 11:34–11:42 window.

maria: Thanks. Keep status updates here. If anyone sees a restore error, ping @oncall-eng immediately. :thumbsup:
